prompt: In a control room, a single industrial alphanumeric pager sits on the edge of a brushed-steel console, its small amber status LED glowing, a coiled rubber antenna and worn belt clip catching a hard directional light from upper-left windows, while deep shadow falls across the empty console. 35mm anamorphic wide shot, shallow depth of field, dramatic falloff, charcoal and safety yellow with bone white highlights, extreme asymmetry with the pager on the lower right third, no people, no text, no logos, fine film grain.

rationale: A cinematic still captures the decisive operational moment in a control room, using one strong practical light and a single recognizable pager to embody the incident budget. It avoids the generic datacenter trope and the sterile macro lens rule for systemic topics.
cue: Your Pager Caps at 2 Incidents a Shift
subject: an industrial alphanumeric pager resting on a control-room console in a dark server operations room
core_thesis: A 24/7 on-call rotation is a fixed staffing machine where two incidents per 12-hour shift and $392 each become the hard budget constraining how many services a team can own.
core_conflict: The fixed incident budget and six-hour cost per incident versus the pressure to onboard more paging services, forcing every new service to draw down finite engineer-hours and payroll.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the pager on the lower right third and dark empty console stretching into negative space on the left
